# Configuration reference

Every configuration key the binary exposes at HEAD, grouped by TOML table.
The page is generated from the registry that backs `trouble config explain`:
the key set, the types and the defaults are read out of the binary, so a key
cannot be resolvable and undocumented at the same time.

* **Keys at HEAD (measured on this tree):** 156
* **TOML tables on this page:** 34
* **Generated by:** `go run ./cmd/trouble config explain --markdown > docs/reference/config.md`
* **Drift gate:** `go test ./internal/lifecycle/ -run TestConfigReference` — fails when the
  registry grows a key this page does not carry, when a meaning outlives its key,
  when a key has no default to print, or when the committed page and the generator
  disagree.

Re-running the generator on this tree produces no diff.

## How to read a row

* **key** — the config key, spelled as the TOML key inside its table.
* **type** — the type of the `Config` field the key sets, read by reflection.
* **default** — the built-in default: what a host with no config file, no
  `TROUBLE_*` variable and no key flag runs. Paths are written as templates
  (`${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}`, `~`) rather than one host's paths, so the
  cell is the same bytes on every host.
* **from** — the layer that supplied the value printed on this page. It reads
  `default` on every row: the page is generated against an absent config file with
  no environment and no key flag, so the built-in default is always what won.
  `trouble config explain` on a configured host reports `file`, `env` or `flag` for
  the keys that host overrides.
* **meaning** — what the key does to the running daemon, not a restatement of its
  name.

Five keys are **declarations** rather than scalars — `projects`, `issues`,
`skills`, `llm` and `sensors.inotify.paths`. They are arrays of tables, they are
marked `file only` in the type column, and a scalar flag or variable cannot
express one (TROUBLE-LIFECYCLE-001).

## Precedence and flag spelling

Quoted from `deploy/README.md`, which is where the precedence sentence is
stated; every other operator doc points here instead of restating it:

> Precedence is flag > env > file > default.

So a key may be set four ways, and the first layer that supplies it wins:
the daemon's `--<flag>`, then its `TROUBLE_*` variable
(see [env-vars.md](env-vars.md)), then a key in this table's TOML section,
then the default on this page.

A key's flag spelling, quoted from `docs/cmd.md` rather than restated:

> any registered key: `a.b_c` → `--a-b_c`

`trouble config explain` accepts only `--state_root` of its own (plus `--key`,
`--json` and `--markdown`); the rest of the flag layer belongs to the daemon.

## Secrets

No credential value appears on this page. A key that names a credential shows
`""` as its default and states in its meaning which environment variable or
file supplies the value; `secrets.environment_file` is the path of the 0600 file
resolution loads variables from, which is an indirection rather than a
credential.

## Top level

Keys written at the root of the config file, outside any table.

| key | type | default | from | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `config_path` | string | `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/trouble/config.toml` | default | The TOML file resolution reads; a path that does not exist is treated as no file at all, not as an error. |
| `health_url` | string | "" | default | URL the stall checker and the upgrade READY wait poll for health; empty derives it from `dashboard.bind`. |
| `issues` | table (file only) | `not declared` | default | The `[issues]` table exactly as declared; core config carries it verbatim and the issues subsystem's own loader is the only judge of its contents. |
| `llm` | table (file only) | `not declared` | default | The agent stage's `[llm]` table exactly as declared; unlike the other subsystem tables a declaration that cannot be built refuses the boot. |
| `projects` | array of tables (file only) | `none declared` | default | The `[[projects]]` declarations: one table per reporter project (id, public_key, optional secret, quota, disk budget, loss policy), and the set the sentinel opens ingest for — an empty set never opens the port. |
| `skills` | table (file only) | `not declared` | default | The `[skills]` table exactly as declared; core config carries it verbatim and the skills loop's own loader is the only judge of its contents. |
| `state_root` | string | `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/trouble` | default | Root of every directory the daemon writes — heartbeat, checker state, spool, plays and the hub's own state — so moving this one key moves all of them. |

## `[secrets]`

| key | type | default | from | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `environment_file` | string | ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/trouble/trouble.env | default | Path of the 0600 env file resolution loads variable values from; the credentials live in that file, and this page carries the path only. |

## `[lifecycle]`

| key | type | default | from | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `checker_unit` | string | `trouble-stall.service` | default | Name of the stall checker's unit, which the daemon restarts when the checker stops probing. |
| `clock_skew_tolerance` | duration | `5s` | default | Skew allowed between the daemon's clock and the timestamps it reads before it treats the difference as an incident. |
| `drain_timeout` | duration | `30s` | default | How long a drain may take before the daemon stops waiting for in-flight work and exits. |
| `escalate_unit` | string | `trouble-escalate@.service` | default | Template unit the escalation ladder instantiates per rung (`trouble-escalate@.service`). |
| `heartbeat_interval` | duration | `30s` | default | How often the daemon rewrites its heartbeat file while it is working. |
| `heartbeat_path` | string | `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/trouble/heartbeat.json` | default | File the daemon rewrites each heartbeat; the checker reads it to decide whether the daemon is alive. |
| `heartbeat_stale_after` | duration | `90s` | default | Age at which the checker calls the heartbeat stale, so it must stay above the heartbeat interval. |
| `idle_heartbeat_interval` | duration | `60s` | default | Heartbeat cadence while the daemon has no work, so an idle daemon still proves it is alive. |
| `rollback_depth` | integer | `2` | default | How many previous binary generations are kept on disk for rollback. |
| `sandbox` | string | `standard` | default | Hardening profile applied to the shipped unit files; `standard` is the documented posture. |
| `self_rss_warn` | string | `80MB` | default | Resident-set size at which the daemon warns about its own memory use, written with a unit suffix (`80MB`). |
| `systemd_scope` | string | `user` | default | Whether the shipped units run under the user manager (`user`) or the system manager (`system`), which decides where `systemctl` looks for them. |
| `unit_name` | string | `trouble.service` | default | Name of the daemon's own unit, used by drain, upgrade and the checker's restart probe. |
| `upgrade_ready_timeout` | duration | `30s` | default | How long an upgrade waits for the new binary to report READY before rolling back. |
| `user` | string | "" | default | Account the units run as under the system manager; empty means the invoking user under the user manager. |
| `watchdog_sec` | duration | `60s` | default | systemd watchdog window the daemon must feed, and the shutdown budget the unit is given on stop. |

## `[dashboard]`

| key | type | default | from | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allow_full` | boolean | `false` | default | Permit the full-timeline gate mode instead of the bounded window. |
| `allow_resume` | boolean | `false` | default | Permit the endpoints that clear a kill-switch, which are otherwise refused. |
| `auth_fail_limit` | integer | `10` | default | Failed authentications allowed per window before the client is refused. |
| `auth_fail_window` | duration | `60s` | default | Window the failed-authentication counter is measured over. |
| `bind` | string | `127.0.0.1:7644` | default | Host:port the dashboard listener binds; a non-loopback bind is what turns the §2.4 exposure checks on. |
| `health_loopback_exempt` | boolean | `true` | default | Answer `/health.json` from the loopback interface without a session, so a local probe does not need a token. |
| `mandate` | string | "" | default | Declared exposure mandate (`proxy` or `tailnet`), required as soon as the bind leaves loopback — the boot refuses without it. |
| `max_body_bytes` | integer | `4096` | default | Largest request body the dashboard accepts before it refuses the POST. |
| `mem_pressure_pct` | integer | `80` | default | Share of the memory high-water mark at which the dashboard sheds poll load instead of growing. |
| `page_limit` | integer | `100` | default | Rows per page and per partial response; the dashboard clamps it at 500. |
| `poll_ms` | integer | `2000` | default | Client poll interval for the console's content partial, in milliseconds. |
| `port` | integer | `7644` | default | Port the dashboard advertises in links and redirects; the listener itself binds `dashboard.bind`. |
| `project_scope` | string array | `[]` | default | Projects a multi-project console may show; required when more than one project is declared and the bind is not loopback. |
| `proxy_cidrs` | string array | `[]` | default | Networks whose forwarding headers are trusted; only consulted when `dashboard.proxy_trusted` is on. |
| `proxy_trusted` | boolean | `false` | default | Trust the forwarding headers of a proxy in front of the dashboard for the client address. |
| `public_origin` | string | "" | default | Exact `scheme://host[:port]` the console is reached on, required off loopback so cookies and links are built against it. |
| `read_only` | boolean | `false` | default | Refuse every mutating request, leaving the console as a viewer. |
| `stall_alert_s` | integer | `90` | default | Age at which the console shows its stale banner because the newest sequence has not moved. |
| `strip_poll_ms` | integer | `1000` | default | Poll interval for the strip accelerator, in milliseconds, so the header refreshes faster than the body. |
| `token_file` | string | "" | default | 0600 store the dashboard API tokens are minted into and read from; the `dashboard token` verbs address this file. |

## `[server.redis]`

| key | type | default | from | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `batch_bytes` | integer | `524288` | default | Byte cap per read request, so a batch of large records is split. |
| `batch_records` | integer | `256` | default | Records per read request. |
| `block_ms` | integer | `1000` | default | How long a read blocks waiting for new records before it returns empty, which trades latency against polling. |

| `claim_min_idle` | duration | `60s` | default | Idle time before a record claimed by a dead consumer is reclaimed by a live one. |
| `consumer` | string | "" | default | Name this instance uses inside the consumer group; empty derives one from the host identity. |
| `dedup_prefix` | string | `trouble:dedup:` | default | Key prefix of the dedup gate, which is what keeps two trouble deployments on one Redis from colliding. |

| `failover_grace` | duration | `30s` | default | How long reconnection is retried before the queue is declared failed. |
| `group` | string | `ledger-writers` | default | Consumer group the queue's readers belong to, which decides how a record is claimed exactly once. |

| `url` | string | "" | default | Redis endpoint the queue and the dedup gate connect to; a password is not part of this value, it comes from `server.redis.password_env`. |

## `[escalate]`

| key | type | default | from | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `channels` | array of string arrays | `[]` | default | The channels an escalation rung runs, one argv per channel; empty means a rung can only be observed, not executed. |
| `timeout` | duration | `10s` | default | How long one escalation channel may run before the rung is treated as failed. |

## `[fs]`

| key | type | default | from | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `forbidden_state_roots` | string array | `/tmp`, `/var/tmp` | default | Filesystem paths the daemon refuses as a state root, because a volatile mount there would lose the ledger on reboot. |
| `remote_types` | string array | `nfs`, `nfs4`, `cifs`, `smb`, `sshfs`, `fuse.sshfs` | default | Filesystem types refused for the state root, because a network mount would put the ledger behind a link that can vanish. |

## `[origin]`

| key | type | default | from | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `host_id` | string | "" | default | Identity stamped on the records this daemon originates, which is how the hub tells two hosts' events apart. |
| `hub_id` | string | "" | default | Hub identity stamped on records that arrived through a hub, so their origin survives a re-forward. |
